summary: The silence broke, and it was mostly an operations week. After three days without a word, the first message back to her was Melissa's agency-wide leak-removal update on 9/25 ('Hey love! Here’s your weekly update on the leak removal breakdown for the past 7 days 🫶🏼'). That ended a 17-day gap in the leak report, and Barbara replied 'Thank you sooo much'. It was a broadcast, though, not a personal reply to the safety question she was left on. She spoke up herself on 9/27 ('hey any update ?? it’s been a couple days now on this 🙏🏼🙏🏼'). Vivek answered 'Starting today', which reads like Meta recovery work only started ten days into the main-account ban. Her follow-up 'Hi' that afternoon got no reply. On 10/1 she was very engaged (about 30 messages). She finished ALTR's new intake form ('finished this :)'). She set out the recovery plan herself: reactivate @barbarasilvanew, change the email, and hand the login to Mayson's VA team so posting can restart. Vivek is appealing @itsbarbxoxo. Derrek closed off last week's login-safety blocker with 'We have this, login, Barbara. Don't worry'. Mica's reel-inspo drop came back on 9/29, and Olivia posted four files into the OFTV topic the same night, the first OFTV activity in about four weeks. What has not changed: her 9/14 retention message ('i really want to continue working together, i just need to see some changes because where the numbers are right now isn’t sustainable for me.') is now 18 days old and nobody has answered it. No plan, no numbers, and the Sep 15 call has never been mentioned again. The main account @thebrazilianfitbarbie has been banned 15 days. Nobody mentioned it all week, nobody has given a date, and she has stopped asking about it. Vivek's replies to her direct questions were mostly non-answers ('Will see', 'Ma'am new guidelines and new system', then 'Yes' to 'what does that mean'). The window closed with three questions of hers unanswered: 'so we followed all the protocols right? no more problems hopefully ?? 🥹', 'then what do we do @fonta' and 'following up on this' (10/2 08:23). She also asked Mayson to 'maybe change the profile picture when you’re in too'. That is the exact action Derrek warned on 9/20 'normally bring the account right back down', and nobody flagged it. Invoice #5 (Sep 15–30) arrived 10/1, two days off cadence, with no heads-up and the pause-of-work clause for the fourth time ('As always, we appreciate you paying within the next 7 days to avoid any pausing in work!'). It was posted 13 minutes after she wrote 'i feel like it keeps going down right after recovery every time', and it bills a fortnight in which her main account was down the whole time. CHURN WATCH: no classic exit signals this window. She did not go quiet or short (39 messages, up from 31), there was no fast payment (invoice #5 is unpaid and not yet due), no requests for exports, logins or data (she is handing logins TO ALTR), and no mention of other agencies. Two softer signs: she deactivated a backup on her own before asking ('Hey so i deactivated my one backup'), and she pushed back on intake-form repetition ('i’ve done a couple intake forms already'). The live exit trigger is unchanged: an 18-day-unanswered retention message meeting an invoice for a period with nothing to show.

health.rationale: Up 7 from 38 (2026-09-25), the first rise since 9/11. The worst fears from last week did not come true. She broke her own silence, stayed cooperative, and finished the intake form. Her login-safety blocker was settled on 10/1: the VA team logs in and Vivek confirmed there is no safety protocol issue. Both proactive services came back in the same week, the leak report (Melissa, 9/25, thanked) and reel inspo (Mica, 9/29). There was a concrete posting plan for @barbarasilvanew by close, and the first OFTV files in about four weeks. The score stays in the 40s for five reasons. (1) The 9/14 retention message is 18 days old and unanswered. Last week said that at 18 days, still unanswered, through the invoice, she should be treated as leaving unless told otherwise. That invoice has now landed. (2) The main account has been banned 15 days with no date, and nobody mentioned it in the window. Last week's 15-day threshold ('the service is not being provided') has been crossed. (3) Meta support quality: 'Starting today' on 9/27 contradicts the 9/22–9/24 progress claims. His replies to her direct questions were 'Will see', 'Ma'am new guidelines and new system' and 'Yes', and the window closed with her 'following up on this' unanswered. (4) The account-hygiene gap caused a live risk: she asked for a profile-picture change on the recovered account and nobody stopped it. (5) Invoice #5 went out two days late with no heads-up and the pause-of-work clause a fourth time, minutes after a distressed message about bans. Churn signals: none of the four classic ones this window (engaged, not short; unpaid not fast-paid; giving logins, not asking for them; no other-agency talk). The risk is structural (the unanswered retention message plus the invoice) rather than behavioural.
